sections.content:
13,815 people

were counted on the census as "upholsterers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Upholsterers upholster vehicle, aircraft and other seating, fix trimmings to the interiors of vehicles and aircraft, upholster furniture such as chairs and sofas, and make mattresses, curtains and other soft furnishings.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "upholsterers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "upholsterers", 14.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "upholsterers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "upholsterers" included:

  • housekeepers and related occupations
  • cleaners and domestics
  • launderers, dry cleaners and pressers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "upholsterers" there were more men than women (70.5% compared with 29.5%).

This means "upholsterers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 70.5% and women made up 29.5% of "upholsterers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "upholsterers" included:

  • other skilled trades
  • photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators
  • estimators, valuers and assessors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "upholsterers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "upholsterers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "upholsterers", 9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (73% compared with 27%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (58.9%) than self-employed (41.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Kirklees, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
